# A route's path is held to the struct that says what its window hands the
# body: every `{name}` names a field, and that field is something a route can
# parse out of text.
#
# Both questions belong to html and not to the checker. A path is a plain
# string until something serves it -- `href` is an ordinary prop on every other
# target, and `{pkg}` is only a placeholder because a route reads it that way.
# The checker asked them anyway, which is the compiler knowing what html knows:
# a window built for bubbletea got a diagnostic about a path nothing routes.
#
# So these are build errors now, and they arrive only for the target that has
# routes. That also makes them reachable by `--lang none`, which serves the
# page as a file: the placeholder is refused there for a different reason
# (route_param_static_refused.txt), so this asks --lang go.
#
# One-directional on purpose: `page` below is a field the path does not name,
# and that is not an error. The path is one source of a request's values and
# the struct is meant to carry the others.

! sngl generate --lang go --platform html -o out-missing missing.sngl
stderr 'the path names \{slug\}, but the window''s params have no field "slug"'

! sngl generate --lang go --platform html -o out-unparseable unparseable.sngl
stderr 'path parameter \{tags\} arrives as text, and field "tags" is list<string>, which a route cannot parse it into'

# The field the path does not name is left alone.
sngl generate --lang go --platform html -o out-ok ok.sngl

-- missing.sngl --
import "sngl:platform/html"
import ui "sngl:ui"

output {
    go {
        html
    }
}

struct PageParams {
    pkg string
    page int
    tags list<string>
}

ui.window #a(title="t", href=`/p/{slug}`, params=PageParams{}) {
    component content(v) {
        html.span(innerText=v.pkg)
    }
}

-- unparseable.sngl --
import "sngl:platform/html"
import ui "sngl:ui"

output {
    go {
        html
    }
}

struct PageParams {
    pkg string
    page int
    tags list<string>
}

ui.window #b(title="t", href=`/t/{tags}`, params=PageParams{}) {
    component content(v) {
        html.span(innerText=v.pkg)
    }
}

-- ok.sngl --
import "sngl:platform/html"
import ui "sngl:ui"

output {
    go {
        html
    }
}

struct PageParams {
    pkg string
    page int
    tags list<string>
}

ui.window #c(title="t", href=`/p/{pkg}`, params=PageParams{}) {
    component content(v) {
        html.span(innerText=v.pkg)
    }
}
